passages.text: Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
passages.sermon:
God is merciful.
I speak to you as brothers and sisters in Christ.
I urge you to respond to God's mercy.
Offer your bodies to God.
Offer your bodies as living sacrifices.
Let your lives be holy.
Let your lives be pleasing to God.
This is your true and spiritual worship.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί διὰ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ παραστῆσαι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν θυσίαν ζῶσαν ἁγίαν τῷ Θεῷ εὐάρεστον τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ὑμῶν

passages.text: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.
passages.sermon:
God is holy and merciful.
God calls you to live differently from the world.
Do not copy the ways of this world.
Let God change you inside.
Let your mind become new.
When your mind is renewed, you will understand God’s will.
God’s will is good.
God’s will pleases Him.
God’s will is perfect.
passages.original: καὶ μὴ συσχηματίζεσθε τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ ἀλλὰ μεταμορφοῦσθε τῇ ἀνακαινώσει τοῦ νοός εἰς τὸ δοκιμάζειν ὑμᾶς τί τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ τὸ ἀγαθὸν καὶ εὐάρεστον καὶ τέλειον

passages.text: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.
passages.sermon:
God gave me grace.
I speak to every one of you because of this grace.
Do not think of yourself more highly than you should.
Think about yourself with sober judgment.
God has given each person a measure of faith.
Judge yourself according to the faith God has given you.
passages.original: Λέγω γὰρ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τῆς δοθείσης μοι παντὶ τῷ ὄντι ἐν ὑμῖν μὴ ὑπερφρονεῖν παρ’ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν ἀλλὰ φρονεῖν εἰς τὸ σωφρονεῖν ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἐμέρισεν μέτρον πίστεως

passages.text: Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function, so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.
passages.sermon:
Each person has one body.
This one body has many parts.
Not all parts of the body do the same thing.
In the same way, we are many people in Christ.
We are one body in Christ.
Each of us is a part of this body.
Each of us belongs to one another.
passages.original: καθάπερ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι πολλὰ μέλη ἔχομεν τὰ δὲ μέλη πάντα οὐ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχει πρᾶξιν οὕτως οἱ πολλοὶ ἓν σῶμά ἐσμεν ἐν Χριστῷ τὸ δὲ καθ’ εἷς ἀλλήλων μέλη

passages.text: We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith; if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach; if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.
passages.sermon:
God gives each of us grace.
God gives us different gifts.
Each person receives a gift from God.
Some people receive the gift of prophecy.
If you have the gift of prophecy, use it according to your faith.
Some people receive the gift of serving.
If you have the gift of serving, then serve.
Some people receive the gift of teaching.
If you have the gift of teaching, then teach.
Some people receive the gift of encouragement.
If you have the gift of encouragement, then encourage others.
Some people receive the gift of giving.
If you have the gift of giving, give generously.
Some people receive the gift of leadership.
If you have the gift of leadership, lead with diligence.
Some people receive the gift of showing mercy.
If you have the gift of showing mercy, do it cheerfully.
passages.original: Ἔχοντες δὲ χαρίσματα κατὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν διάφορα εἴτε προφητείαν κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς πίστεως εἴτε διακονίαν ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ εἴτε ὁ διδάσκων ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ εἴτε ὁ παρακαλῶν ἐν τῇ παρακλήσει ὁ μεταδιδοὺς ἐν ἁπλότητι ὁ προϊστάμενος ἐν σπουδῇ ὁ ἐλεῶν ἐν ἱλαρότητι

passages.text: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.
passages.sermon:
Love must be sincere.
Do not pretend to love.
Hate what is evil.
Hold tightly to what is good.
passages.original: Ἡ ἀγάπη ἀνυπόκριτος ἀποστυγοῦντες τὸ πονηρόν κολλώμενοι τῷ ἀγαθῷ

passages.text: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Rome.
He tells them how to live as followers of Jesus.
Show deep love to each other as brothers and sisters.
Care for one another with real affection.
Honor each other more than you honor yourselves.
Try to give more respect to others than you receive.
passages.original: τῇ φιλαδελφίᾳ εἰς ἀλλήλους φιλόστοργοι τῇ τιμῇ ἀλλήλους προηγούμενοι

passages.text: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
passages.sermon: Christians must not become lazy in their zeal.\r\nThey must keep their spiritual fervor strong.\r\nThey must serve the Lord.
passages.original: τῇ σπουδῇ μὴ ὀκνηροί τῷ πνεύματι ζέοντες τῷ Κυρίῳ δουλεύοντες

passages.text: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Rome.
He tells them how to live as followers of Jesus.
He says, "Be joyful in hope."
He says, "Be patient in affliction."
He says, "Be persistent in prayer."
passages.original: τῇ ἐλπίδι χαίροντες τῇ θλίψει ὑπομένοντες τῇ προσευχῇ προσκαρτεροῦντες

passages.text: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.
passages.sermon:
Christians must help other believers who have needs.
Christians must share what they have with these believers.
Christians must always look for chances to show hospitality.
Christians must welcome others into their homes and lives.
passages.original: ταῖς χρείαις τῶν ἁγίων κοινωνοῦντες τὴν φιλοξενίαν διώκοντες

passages.text: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Rome.
He tells them how to treat others.
Some people will persecute you.
Bless those people.
Do not curse them.
Bless them instead.
passages.original: Εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς διώκοντας ὑμᾶς εὐλογεῖτε καὶ μὴ καταρᾶσθε

passages.text: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
passages.sermon: Christians must care for others.\r\nRejoice with people who rejoice.\r\nWeep with people who weep.
passages.original: χαίρειν μετὰ χαιρόντων κλαίειν μετὰ κλαιόντων

passages.text: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Rome.
He tells them how to live with each other.
Live in harmony with one another.
Do not be proud.
Spend time with humble people.
Do not think you are wise in your own eyes.
passages.original: τὸ αὐτὸ εἰς ἀλλήλους φρονοῦντες μὴ τὰ ὑψηλὰ φρονοῦντες ἀλλὰ τοῖς ταπεινοῖς συναπαγόμενοι μὴ γίνεσθε φρόνιμοι παρ’ ἑαυτοῖς

passages.text: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Rome.
He teaches how to live as followers of Jesus.
Do not repay anyone evil for evil.
Do not return harm when someone harms you.
Think carefully about what is good.
Do what is right in the eyes of all people.
passages.original: μηδενὶ κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἀποδιδόντες προνοούμενοι καλὰ ἐνώπιον πάντων ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to Christians in Rome.
He told them how to live with others.
If it is possible for you, live at peace with everyone.
Do your part to make peace with all people.
passages.original: εἰ δυνατόν τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν μετὰ πάντων ἀνθρώπων εἰρηνεύοντες

passages.text: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
passages.sermon:
Beloved, do not take revenge for yourselves.
Let God handle anger and judgment.
God has said, “Vengeance belongs to Me.”
God says, “I will repay.”
passages.original: μὴ ἑαυτοὺς ἐκδικοῦντες ἀγαπητοί ἀλλὰ δότε τόπον τῇ ὀργῇ γέγραπται γάρ Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω λέγει Κύριος

passages.text: On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to Christians in Rome.
He taught them how to treat their enemies.
If your enemy is hungry, give him food.
If your enemy is thirsty, give him something to drink.
When you do this, you show kindness to your enemy.
By showing kindness, you will heap burning coals on his head.
This means your kindness may lead your enemy to feel shame and change his ways.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ Ἐὰν πεινᾷ ὁ ἐχθρός σου ψώμιζε αὐτόν ἐὰν διψᾷ πότιζε αὐτόν τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν ἄνθρακας πυρὸς σωρεύσεις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
passages.sermon:
Evil exists in the world.
Evil can try to defeat you.
Do not let evil defeat you.
Do not let evil control you.
Goodness is powerful.
Use goodness to fight evil.
Defeat evil by doing good.
passages.original: Μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ ἀλλὰ νίκα ἐν τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν
